newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ZEMAN TO PROPOSE CONFIDENCE VOTE ON GOVT.
newsitem.headline: ZEMAN TO PROPOSE CONFIDENCE VOTE ON GOVT.

text.p: Milos Zeman, the head of the largest Czech opposition party the Social Democrats (CSSD), said on Friday that his party would move for a vote of no confidence in the centre-right government in the session of parliament which begins on July 1.

The announcement follows the Wednesday unveiling of the government's emergency austerity programme which was aimed at stabilising the Czech currency, the crown, after two weeks of intense downward pressure.

"The government diverted in a major way from its (original) programme declaration," Zeman, who is chairman of the lower house, told a news conference as the reason why the motion would be put forward.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's three party coalition, which holds 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house, agreed on Wednesday to sharp budget cuts, public sector wage freezes, and other belt-tightening measures while saying that mistakes were made in their economic policy.

The finance, industry and trade, education and interior ministers were changed as part of the Wednesday shakeup. Ivan Pilip, part of Klaus's inner circle, was named to replace Ivan Kocarnik as finance minister, whom many Czechs blamed for the economic problems.
Zeman said he was not pushing for early elections but "a real reconstruction, not comic swaps of portfolios"
